end.summary:
Practised physical and chemical changes using melting/freezing ghee or ice, folding paper, burning paper, rusting, and cooking chapati.
Ananya identified that physical changes do not form a new substance and can often be reversed.
They identified burning paper and rusting as chemical changes because new substances form.
They remained unsure whether roasting chapati is physical or chemical; this was not corrected by the final turn.
Teach-back was not passed; no unaided correct responses were recorded.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the idea of checking whether a new substance forms, using familiar examples such as folded paper, melted ghee, rust, and cooked chapati. Ananya explained several examples by focusing on whether the original material could return, and connected rusting with a new substance. They mixed up the chapati example because it cannot return to raw dough, and this was not resolved before the lesson ended. At home, ask Ananya to sort household examples into physical or chemical changes and give one reason for each.
